links.reason: 2939 says 'we die from the day we are born' (இனிச்செத்தாம் பிறந்த போழ்தே) and 2616 says we do not know our span and weep only when the cow is milked (கறந்துகூற் றுண்ணு ஞான்று); the two share the theme of life's brevity but neither verse echoes the other's words, so 'passed down' doctrine is the marker's story, not the Tamil. Pairing is thematic agreement, not development.
links.text_issue: 2939 line 4 is compressed and flagged uncertain; line 3 தனிச்சித்தம் வைத்தறேற்றாம் is hard

links.reason: Both are the woman telling her friend the promised rains have come (காரே வந்தன்று / கார்மன் இதுவால்) while he is absent, so the situation is shared and 'parallel domain' (a different field) does not fit. The claim about colophon thinai cues rests on the colophon labels, not on anything in the verses beyond 183's mention of the waste (அத்தம்ஆர் அழுவம்).

820 states the sin of the battlefield is put away (போர்கெழு களத்துப் பாவம் புலம்பொடு போக்கினானே) with image, festival and gifts; 2357 only has worship, flung gold and putting on ornaments, with no word of sin or expiation. Reading 2357 as 'the same rite of expiation' is the marker's inference, not the verse.

29 says Civakan no longer wants the pleasure of women having tasted a greater sweetness; 2806 says the gods watch goddesses dance and 'திருவொடு திளைத்து மானார்', where மானார் is itself uncertain. The verse does not say the gods are unsatisfied, so it cannot supply 'the reason' for the turn in 29.
links.text_issue: 2806 line 4 மானார் read as 'not satisfied' by the marker, not stated

links.reason: Both use ஏதிலர்/ஏதிலார் but make no incompatible claim: 1130 says the town calls him a stranger while he dwells in her heart, 1300 says it is no wonder strangers are not kin when one's own heart is not. Shared word only; 'the outsider is inside' is not a stated teaching.

1840 has the royal assembly (வேத்தவை) declare Civakan the one master of elephants; 1121 has Kattiyangaran threaten to write 'thief' with a tusk (கள்வர் என்ன எழுதுவித்திடுவல்). These are two reactions in different episodes, not incompatible claims, and the Tamil does not say the assembly's king is lawful or that the elephant is the same.

638 is about a minister's duty to speak to a king who destroys counsel (அறிகொன்று); in 146 the king listens (நரபதியுங் கேட்டனன்), so the note's premise of a king who will not listen is wrong. The 'false premise' teaching needs the queen to be alive, which the verse does not say.

294 shows Kattiyankaran weeping and joining hands (கைதொழுதான் கண்ணீர்) over the king; 2144 has his letter protest false blame (பொய்ப்பழி). The pair is a real contrast but not a shared image, and 'Govindan sees through the letter at once' is not in either verse.

265 looses the hounds on the ascetic; 279 says they do not come near (ஞமலி யிவை நணுகல) and the killing karma has stopped joining the king, so the later verse reverses the earlier. That is a within-epic answer, not incompatible claims; 'before his remorse begins' is outside the verses.

134 has the merchant say he does not know why the five hundred sing (காரணம் யானறியேன்); 137 gives the women's city and Vayuvegan's demand for his nephew but does not say why they sing. 'The marvel becomes a wrong the hero will put right' is not stated in either verse.

1360 has a simile (நல்லுயிர் போவதேபோல், as a good life leaves the body) for his going; 1122 says the bond is that of body and life, so the image is shared. But the verse does not make the wife's state a death, so 'the husband's going is a death for the wife' goes beyond the Tamil (1364 shows only lament).

Titles check: குணவதன், குணப்பெருங் கோமான், தேவன் and சங்கரன் ஈசன் சயம்பு are in 181-186, against ஓவாது நின்ற குணத்து and தேவாதி தேவன் in CC 1. Both praise the Jina by his qualities, but the verses limit nothing in each other, and 'two strategies' is a contrast drawn from one verse of the Cintamani.

Both are a woman speaking to a household bird (பூவை / கிளி), a real shared figure, but no claim conflicts. 1364 has Padumai reproach the myna only; the swan, peacock and lamp, and the parrot flying as envoy, are not in these verses, and 1000 has the parrot only ask her to name the man.
links.text_issue: 1000 speech division is the marker's reading (என்றதே)

links.reason: 2623 bids those who see diners in gold bowls not to think wealth theirs but to think of austerity (செல்வம் நமரங்காண் நினையன்மின் செய்தவமே நினைமின்); ND 273 mocks the hoarder who neither enjoys nor gives to renunciants (துறவோர்க்கொன் றீகலான்). ND says nothing of penance, and the banquet-table 'temptation of ease' is not in the quatrain.

698 forbids belittling a king by his youth or kin degree (இளையர் இனமுறையர் என்றிகழார்); 212 has Pradyotan plead the uncle-nephew tie (மாமனான் மருகன் நீ). That the king 'wronged his kinsman' and is 'the stronger party' is reconstructed plot, and the first line is hard to construe.
links.text_issue: line 1 hard to construe; flagged uncertain

links.reason: 2240 has warriors who have paid the debt of the red rice (செஞ்சோற்றுக் கடனீங்கி) with jackals howling; 780 praises a death that fills the patron's eyes with tears. A verse that simply does not mention the patron has not 'removed' him, and 780 is not about a debt of rice, so the Kural gives no frame the verse lacks.

79 says the princes' youth kindles love-sickness in women (காமநோய் எரிவளைத்திடுவதோர் இளமை); TM 180 is one man's recollection of being cane-sweet and now bitter. The princes' blaze is not the speaker's earlier stage, so 'one curve' is imposed from outside both texts.
links.text_issue: TM 180 prints only three lines in the packet

links.reason: 1186 proposes that men fight men without trickery (வஞ்சனை யின்றி மக்கள் பொருபவேன்); PN 9 has the Pandya spare cows, brahmins, women, the sick and the sonless before shooting (எம்அம்பு கடிவிடுதும்). Both limit war but the limits differ, so 'qualifies' is only a shared theme and neither side is said to gain.

2388 seats drummers on an elephant to beat the wedding drum (கடிமுரசு அறைவான்); ND 86 has drums beaten for many to know. The astrologer's day and the seven days of orders are not in 2388, and the epic verse says nothing of the husband's fidelity, so this is an illustration.

2371 is purely a scene of the lion throne and crowned kings (சிங்காசனத்தின்மேல் ... மன்னர் முடிகள் சூழ); ND 3 says kings who rode under the umbrella fall when their deeds turn. Nothing in 2371 hints at a fall or a warning, so reading it as one turn of a wheel is imported.

1217 names Civakan by the earlier act (செல்கதி மந்திரம் செவியிற் செப்பிய) and 945 shows him whispering the mantras into the dog's ear (செவிச் செப்புகின்றான்), so the later gift answers the earlier compassion. That the dog became the god is not in either verse but is what 1217's வாழ நாட்டவே implies.

273 uses வேண்டாமை வேண்டிய தெல்லாம் தரும் for a king's servant who asks for nothing, while 363 calls வேண்டாமை the finest wealth with nothing like it. The pair shows the same word moved from renouncer's ethics to courtly method, which neither shows alone.

560 says the cows' yield fails when the guardian does not guard (ஆபயன் குன்றும் ... காவலன் காவான் எனின்); 429 shows only the king fanned on his throne, and the raid is in other verses. It illustrates the Kural, and the couplet is not about raids.
links.text_issue: 429 does not name the king or the herds

links.reason: 330 lists make dharma, drop anger (வெகுளி போக்குக), look to knowledge, guard the vow; 360 names காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம் as what must perish. Only anger is shared, so the verse does not 'name the practices that make the three perish' and the two do not qualify each other.

236 says the unrewarded petitioner is not to be called dull or small because gain comes by lot (நோற்றார்க்குச் சோற்றுள்ளும் வீழும் கறி), and 618 says lacking fortune is no one's disgrace (பொறியின்மை யார்க்கும் பழியன்று). The pair shows the Kural's line on blame used to shield a petitioner, while 618 still names slackness as the disgrace.

1827 has the kings calm themselves that deeds ripen not as one wishes (வேண்டிய வாறு வாரா வினை); 1839 says wealth and heavenly pleasure are the fruit of deeds (வினையதனின் விளைவின்ன தென்று). Same doctrine, but 1839 is about reward not loss, and that the scene was 'built to carry' it is the marker's claim.

Pattupattu 218-228 does cross the tracts (குறிஞ்சி பரதவர் பாட நெய்தல் ... குறவர் சூட) and ends in one umbrella (ஒருகுடையான்), against 33 where each woman keeps her tract's flower. The contrast is true, but the 'gains' are invented: nothing in 33 supplies the realm's unity, and the Pattupattu gains nothing from the verse; 'ends in a catalogue' is not shown.

225 has the king leave the fallen tree unexplained (பின்னதனால் பயன் பேசலன் விட்டான்) and 267 has him say all she dreamed has come to pass (கனவு எல்லாம் விளைந்த), so the later verse admits the part he withheld. A dream and its fulfilment, answered in the Tamil.

ND 16 has a lamb nibbling the garland in the slaughter ground (மறிகுளகுண்டன்ன); YK 20 only lists pairs of peacocks, cocks, pigs, goats and buffaloes brought together. No sacrifice, garland or unawareness is said, so there is no shared image.

Both verses carry the same simile, சிலந்தி நூல் ... சிங்கம்போல் (the lion bound in a spider's thread), for Udayanan's seizure, once as narrator and once in Pradyotan's letter. The echo of one distinctive figure across two parts of the poem is real and tells a reader the captor's letter borrows the poem's own image.

2840 says they are bound by the garland of desire (காமத் தொங்கலாற் பிணிக்கப்பட்டார்); 2610 says Saccandan was swallowed by pleasure (போகத்தால் விழுங்கப்பட்டு). Both say pleasure binds, so there is no incompatibility; 2610 does not say that pleasure is the fruit of merit.

Both use a cart wheel (சகடத் துருளும் / சகடக்கால் போல், ND 2), but for different things: the soul in 1921, wealth in ND 2. The 'lesser double' and 'larger turning behind' are not in either text, since ND 2 does not mention deeds.

678 is about using an elephant to bind an elephant (யானையால் யானையாத்தற்று); in 85 Yugi whispers to the king's elephant and it breaks its chain. The elephant is the tool, not a captor of another elephant, and the note's 'price in lives' is only the mantra's command to destroy the army and city.

1584 has the opened flesh with crows at the eyes (கண்ணுட் காக்கை), ND 41 the torn skin needing a stick to drive away crows; the carrion image is shared. But 1584's lines 2-3 are uncertain, and the Naladiyar gains nothing from a later use of its figure.

1669 sends the king to the pool to watch the women (ஆடல் காண்பான்) and 1674 has them start a water-fight against him, so the watcher becomes a target. That is the next step of one scene, which the plot already records, not a fulfilment of a claim or sign.

1628 closes with the sweetness of sweet-smiling sons' wealth (இன்னகைப் புதல்வர் செல்வம்) after a wedding of plants; Kural 63 says children are called wealth because their wealth comes by their own deeds. The verse never says the joy rests on rearing rather than deeds, so the 'test' of the couplet is read in.

347 says a deed of a former birth (உம்மை நின்றது ஓர் ஊழ்வினை) made her suffer and she reached the hermitage; it does not say she renounces, and the later grief inside the hermitage is not in the verse. The Kural does not 'answer in the negative' any question about tapas ending suffering.

106 has an astrologer relate a dream of a garlanding elephant; Siddhar 529 says all seen has become a dream (கனவாச்சே கண்டதெல்லாம்). They share the word dream, but one dream is an omen and the other a figure for unreality; no claim is incompatible.

1981 says the pair became one life in two bodies because they never parted (விட்டு நீங்குதல் இன்மையின் ... ஈருடம்போருயி ராயினார்); 1122 is body and life. The images differ, the departure in 1994 is not in the packet, and the Kural's 'pledge' is not the verse's condition.

233 tells the king to build one rare machine (ஓர் அரும் பொறி புனைவி) and 272 says the vehicle is ready (ஊர்தி சமைந்தது), an order and its fulfilment. 'Penance' for lust and 'saving the heir' are not said in either verse, so the teaching is partly the marker's.

531 ranks slackness born of great joy above anger as a cause of ruin; in 47 the king walks on despite birds and omens (புள்ளிடை தடுப்ப) and only grows glad after seeing the decoy elephant (இனியனானான்), so the heedlessness precedes the joy. The couplet is not shown at work.

141 has the king lament over burnt ornaments in place of a body; TM 145 describes the town burying a real corpse and forgetting him. The 'unfinished grief' of the king is not in 141, and the doctrine of transience in the Tirumanthiram gains nothing from a staged death.

2701 shows women pale-lipped and thin-shouldered after play (செவ்வாய் விளர்த்துத் தோண்மெலிந்து) and sinking onto the bed; ND 17 warns that the spear-eyed beauty will stoop with a staff. Weariness after love is not an 'early decline', so the Naladiyar's argument from age is not touched.
